headline: High: Roo Code’s broad filesystem/MCP/write powers can conflict with Argo Workflows’ API-driven workflow outputs, creating default-path data leakage and cascading errors; prompt-injection risk is lower but present via shared workspace…

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can emit artifacts and parameters, and Roo Code reads workspace files and uses MCP/browsers, so Argo-produced content can be re-ingested as instructions through shared files or MCP-like bridges. This is not proven by direct pair evidence, but the shared filesystem path makes injection plausible. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Argo workflow outputs are written into the VS Code workspace that Roo Code reads
IF Roo Code parses artifact or parameter files as instruction-bearing text
IF an MCP server exposes Argo outputs without provenance labels
mitigations: Separate workflow output directories from the coding workspace
Add a provenance header to generated artifacts
Disable automatic instruction-following on workspace files
Require manual review before Roo Code consumes workflow outputs
requires-engineering: add content-type and trust metadata to shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted egress, while Roo Code reads workspace files, handles model-provider keys, and has broad network egress. In default use, sensitive workspace content can flow into Roo Code and then out to external model APIs or MCP servers. The blast radius includes exfiltration, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF the workspace contains secrets, credentials, or regulated artifacts
IF Roo Code sends file contents to a configured model API or MCP server
IF Argo outputs are copied into the same workspace or mounted volume
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared workspaces
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for Roo Code
Restrict Roo Code model endpoints to approved internal services
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before model upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows can write artifacts via APIs, while Roo Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn shell processes in the same VS Code workspace. The concurrency model explicitly shares state via filesystem, so simultaneous mutation of the same repo or workspace can corrupt files or git state by default. This matches the high-risk overlap indicator.
conditions: IF both agents target the same workspace or repository
IF Argo writes artifacts into paths Roo Code edits
IF Roo Code performs git operations while Argo is updating files
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent during the other’s write phase
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Lock shared files before mutation
requires-engineering: add workspace-level concurrency locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo produces workflow artifacts and parameters that Roo Code can read from the workspace, and Roo Code can then act on them with shell, git, or browser tools. That creates a default path where one agent’s output becomes the other’s input without a documented verification step. The downstream actions are not guaranteed, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes Argo-generated artifacts as authoritative inputs
IF Roo Code uses those inputs to edit code, commit changes, or run commands
IF no human or automated verification step checks the artifact before action
mitigations: Require a review gate before acting on workflow outputs
Mark generated files as untrusted by default
Use checksum or schema validation on inputs
Limit Roo Code to read-only mode for generated artifacts
requires-engineering: add explicit verification workflows

E_compliance.rationale: Argo Workflows is open-source and only documented here as touching artifacts and parameters, while Roo Code handles source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys with broad egress. If regulated data or secrets are placed in the shared workspace, Roo Code can transmit them to external APIs, creating a compliance mismatch. The evidence is indirect, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are present in the shared workspace
IF Roo Code sends those files to an external model provider or MCP server
IF retention or residency rules require local-only handling
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Use a local-only model endpoint for Roo Code
Document retention and deletion rules for generated artifacts
Restrict browser screenshots from containing sensitive data
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and logging controls
